Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent overhead foliage sprite for an existing hand-painted 2D top-down game. Image 1 is a close crop of the ACTUAL TERRAIN FOLIAGE whose look we must match. Image 2 is wider terrain context. Preserve the first reference's specific broad rounded paddle/spoon-shaped leaves, simple central veins, softly textured painted surface, warm lime/olive/moss hues, dark leaf-over-leaf undersides, and strongly top-down 70–80 degree camera. The user prefers these leaves to our previous thin upright twig shrubs. Create one complete isolated LOW, WIDE, DENSE clump of this exact kind of foliage on genuine transparent alpha. Broad leaves radiate outward and overlap each other in 2–3 layers, with large readable individual leaf faces, not lots of tiny detail. Crown mostly hidden beneath leaves. No upright trunk or tall exposed stalks, no front/eye-level view. Soft upper-left light matching the reference. Whole natural irregular silhouette inside the frame with at least 10% transparent margin; all leaf tips intact. No ground tile, no dirt disk, stones, cobbles, moss carpet, cast shadow on ground, label, text, frames or unrelated objects. Keep darker contact shading ONLY between the leaves, not a backdrop. The final sprite must read as if the leafy plant has been lifted out of the terrain, ready to place seamlessly back onto it.
Subject: a full low mound of 18–22 very broad rounded olive and moss-green leaves, with lime-green younger leaves near the center and a few warm ochre tips. Match the central broadleaf plant in Image 1 closely. Leaf faces are large, oval and spoon-shaped; almost no stem is visible. A few medium lower leaves spread toward viewer to give a cushion-like silhouette. Approximately 1.35 times wider than tall. Green foliage only, no flowers.
